finding: The entire cart runtime is injected only into the SINGLE-FILE export and never into a published page, so Add-to-Cart is dead on every live site for a second reason independent of the one already filed as W-O-26.
evidence: generateStripeScripts has exactly one call site repo-wide: ExportEngine.ts:544, inside wrapInDocument. wrapInDocument is private and reached only from generateHTML (ExportEngine.ts:217,220,227), i.e. the export()/single-file path. The publish path is exportPublishPages.ts:39 -> exportAllPages -> exportPageToHtml (ExportEngine.ts:805-887), whose head assembly emits fonts, SEO, stylesheet link, globalCss, headScripts, analytics (:858) and the interaction runtime (:864) and never calls generateStripeScripts. generateZip (:1103) also routes through exportAllPages, so the ZIP misses it too. The button ships regardless: ProductCard.tsx:32 <button data-add-to-cart>, and data-* attributes survive the export sanitiser (sanitization.ts:118,135 ALLOW_DATA_ATTR defaults true). window.AquibraCart and the only [data-add-to-cart] click binding live inside generateCartScript, reachable only via generateStripeScripts (StripeInjector.ts:207-231,250).
fix: Read the cart config from project settings inside exportPageToHtml the way analytics already is (ExportEngine.ts:858 reads composer.getProjectSettings().analytics rather than the never-populated export-config field), so publish and single-file emit the same head. Until an editor surface writes StripeConfig (W-O-26), stop shipping an Add to Cart button in the Product Card block.
chain: Publish -> StripeConfig -> generateStripeScripts -> (no call in exportPageToHtml) -> Published page -> cart runtime absent, Add-to-Cart button inert

finding: One Export modal produces two different sites: 'Download HTML' is the ACTIVE PAGE only and carries the cart scripts, while 'Download .zip' is every page and does not — the two buttons disagree on both page count and feature set.
evidence: ExportModal.tsx:77 calls engine.export() -> generateHTML -> getActivePage (ExportEngine.ts:216) -> wrapInDocument, which emits Stripe (:544). ExportModal.tsx:125 calls engine.generateZip(config) -> exportAllPages (ExportEngine.ts:1103) -> exportPageToHtml, which does not. Same modal, same config object, two artifacts.
fix: Make exportPageToHtml the single head writer for all three paths (single-file, ZIP, publish) and have wrapInDocument delegate to it, or at minimum move the Stripe/cart injection to the shared point so the three cannot drift again.
chain: Export -> ExportConfig -> Download HTML vs Download .zip -> ExportEngine -> two different documents from one modal

finding: exportProject()'s hardcoded assets:[] does NOT reach the publish path — publish reads the live element tree, not the project snapshot — so the media LIBRARY is what fails to survive a reload, not the images on the page.
evidence: Composer.ts:604-616 exportProject() returns assets: []. The publish payload does not use it: exportPublishPages.ts:39 -> exportAllPages -> composer.elements.exportPages() (ExportEngine.ts:642-645), and page HTML is written from element attributes (renderPageElement, ExportEngine.ts:1010-1050). exportProject() IS the payload for the server save (Composer.ts:506,536), for named versions (VersionTimelineManager.ts:657,984) and for local storage (StorageAdapter.ts:50), so the AssetData[] declared on ProjectData (shared/types/project.ts:44) is written empty every time. MediaManager.ts:1081 already names this in a comment.
fix: Either populate assets from MediaManager in exportProject() or delete the field from ProjectData — a declared-but-always-empty entity is what makes the media library look persisted when it is not. Publish behaviour is unaffected either way; the risk is a restored version or a reloaded project showing an empty library over pages that still reference the files.
chain: Publish -> ProjectData.assets -> exportProject() -> server save / version restore -> Media library -> library empty on reload while page images still reference the URLs

finding: SITE_PUBLISHED does have one listener, but it is only the onboarding checklist tick — the Published version list never refreshes, so publishing with the History panel open leaves the just-shipped version invisible and the 'live version' banner naming the previous one.
evidence: Emitted at AquibraStudio.tsx:446. The only listener in src/ is OnboardingMount.tsx:64 ({ id: 'publish', event: EVENTS.SITE_PUBLISHED }), and OnboardingMount is mounted (AquibraStudio.tsx:743) — so the graph's 'weak' classification for SITE_PUBLISHED (EVENT-GRAPH.json) is right and 'no listener' is not. PublishHistory, the component the History panel's Published view mounts (HistoryTab.tsx:362), reloads only on siteId change: load is useCallback with deps [siteId] (PublishHistory.tsx:158,177) and the effect is [load] (:179); the only other reload is rollback completion. Its liveVersion/nextVersion are derived from rows[0] (:154-156), so a stale list mis-states which version is live. The Publish PANEL does refresh — PublishTab.tsx:177 passes publishJob?.uiState as usePublishSnapshot's reloadKey — which is exactly the wiring PublishHistory lacks.
fix: Subscribe PublishHistory to EVENTS.SITE_PUBLISHED (it already takes a composer-adjacent context via HistoryTab) and call load(), the same way PublishTab keys its snapshot on uiState.
chain: Publish -> PublishBuildJob COMPLETED -> SITE_PUBLISHED -> History panel (Published view) -> PublishHistory.load() -> new version row appears and the live-version banner is correct

finding: There is no failure counterpart to SITE_PUBLISHED anywhere in the editor bus, so a publish that fails is invisible to every module outside the one React subtree that polled it.
evidence: grep of packages/editor/src for SITE_PUBLISH_FAILED returns nothing; the name exists only as a dashboard notification type (lib/constants/enums.ts:134,235) and in the server comment publish.service.ts:360. events.ts declares SITE_PUBLISHED (:229) with no failure sibling. The failure is known — usePublishJob resolves uiState 'failed' and useExportHandlers toasts it — but it is React state, not an event, so History, Review, Pages and onboarding cannot distinguish 'never published' from 'publish just failed'.
fix: Declare and emit SITE_PUBLISH_FAILED beside the SITE_PUBLISHED emit (AquibraStudio.tsx:446 already has the uiState it needs), carrying jobId and error, so panels can show a recovery affordance instead of the idle state.
chain: Publish -> PublishBuildJob FAILED -> (no event) -> History / Review / Pages -> panels show 'never published' over a site whose publish just failed

finding: The three Export events are declared and emitted by nothing, so a code export — the module's other user-visible verb — leaves no trace on the bus at all.
evidence: events.ts:406-408 declares EXPORT_START, EXPORT_COMPLETE, EXPORT_ERROR. A grep of packages/editor/src for all three (constant name, not call site) returns only events.ts. EVENT-GRAPH.json lists all three in its 'never' set of 82. The export path instead toasts locally (useExportHandlers.ts:87-99).
fix: Either emit them from ExportEngine's three outcomes so History/onboarding can record 'exported the site', or delete the three constants — a declared event nobody emits is indistinguishable from a feature that was never built.
chain: Export -> ZIP produced -> (no event) -> History / onboarding -> no record that the user ever exported

finding: Review does not react to a publish, so a round the client approved keeps reading 'Approved' with no indication that the approved work has actually shipped.
evidence: grep of src/editor/sidebar/tabs/review for SITE_PUBLISHED, publishJob or isPublished returns nothing. The server already models the relationship — publish-approval.ts:59-64 isApprovalStale compares the review's resolvedAt against the site's lastEditedAt — so 'approved and shipped' vs 'approved and not yet shipped' is a distinction the data supports and the panel never draws.
fix: Have ReviewTab listen for SITE_PUBLISHED and stamp the approved round as shipped, so the client-facing state ends at 'live' rather than at 'approved'.
chain: Publish -> ReviewRequest APPROVED -> SITE_PUBLISHED -> Review panel -> round marked shipped instead of sitting on 'Approved' forever

finding: Forms survive publish only because the SERVER rescues them — the engine ships an actionless <form> — so the same form in a DOWNLOADED export posts nowhere, and a missing NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL hard-fails the whole publish.
evidence: collectFormElements only records a form when formConfig.webhookUrl is set (ExportEngine.ts:890-915, gate at :909), and FormspreeInjector.processHTML skips any form whose action resolves to null (FormspreeInjector.ts:82-88). So a form built in the editor leaves the engine with no action. The rescue is entirely dashboard-side: planFormWiring (lib/publish-forms.ts:132) points every actionless form at the public endpoint and the worker upserts the FormBlock row (worker route.ts:315-345). That rescue runs on the publish payload only — generateZip and export() never touch it. publish-forms.ts:138-148 also refuses the publish outright when appOrigin is empty. engine/forms is one of the 7 isolated modules in EVENT-GRAPH.json, consistent with this.
fix: Move the actionless-form default into ExportEngine so the downloaded export and the published site agree, or state plainly in the export modal that forms only work on a published Buildrik site.
chain: Publish -> form element -> ExportEngine (no action) -> dashboard worker planFormWiring -> live form works; same element -> Download .zip -> no rescue -> form posts nowhere

finding: A ZIP export whose images all fail to download reports 'Export complete' and hands the user an archive with no assets — bundleAssets returns its errors and the caller throws them away.
evidence: AssetBundler.bundleAssets deliberately collects per-URL failures into an errors array rather than swallowing them (AssetBundler.ts:180-198, and the comment at :129-132 says fetchAssetOrThrow exists so failures can be surfaced). Both call sites destructure only the assets: ExportEngine.ts:1109 and :1111 (`const { assets: imageAssets } = await bundler.bundleAssets(imageUrls)`). generateZip then proceeds and resolves normally, so useExportHandlers.ts:88-94 fires the unconditional success toast.
fix: Return the errors from generateZip and let the caller toast 'Exported — N images could not be downloaded' with the list. The failure mode is realistic: bundleAssets fetches with mode:'cors' (AssetBundler.ts:153) against a blob host the page does not control.
chain: Export -> asset URLs -> bundleAssets errors -> (discarded at ExportEngine.ts:1109) -> Export modal -> 'Export complete' over an archive with broken images

finding: The pre-publish checklist describes the last SAVED site while the deploy carries the LIVE editor tree, and the checklist is never re-read on an edit — so it can block or bless a state that is not the one about to ship.
evidence: runPrePublishChecks counts pages from prisma.page (publish.service.ts:27-31,60-72) — server rows. The payload is built from the live tree with no save first: useExportHandlers.ts:118 calls exportPublishPages(composer) and goes straight to publishJob.publish, and grep of that file for save/flush finds nothing. PublishTab re-reads the checks only on mount and after a publish settles (PublishTab.tsx:287-298), never on an edit. Autosave narrows the window to roughly THRESHOLDS.AUTOSAVE_DEBOUNCE = 1000ms (config.ts:113) for content edits, so the common case is fine; the panel-left-open case is not. Only 'fail' blocks (PublishTab.tsx:308 blockedByChecks).
fix: Re-read the checks on the same signal usePublishSnapshot already subscribes to (HISTORY_RECORDED and friends, usePublishSnapshot.ts:135-145), or run the checks against the payload the client is about to send rather than the saved rows.
chain: Publish -> pre-publish checks -> prisma.page (saved) vs exportPublishPages (live) -> Publish panel -> checklist grades a different site from the one that deploys

finding: VERIFIED SURVIVES — CMS content and dynamic collection pages both reach the published site; the export default was corrected to 'static' and the server appends generated detail pages.
evidence: Publish resolves bindings by default: cmsOptions mode is options.cmsMode ?? 'static' (ExportEngine.ts:700-704) and each page is passed through cmsResolver.resolve (:709-712). The single-file path resolves too (ExportEngine.ts:185-188), so the two agree. Dynamic pages are added server-side: appendDynamicPagesToPublish (cms.service.ts:229-246) expands every CmsCollection with a pageSlugPattern and pageTemplatePath against the template page's HTML, and is imported by publish.service.ts:5.
fix: None. Recorded so the next pass does not re-derive it.
chain: Publish -> CMS bindings + collections -> CMSExportResolver (static) + appendDynamicPagesToPublish -> Published site -> entries and detail pages present

finding: VERIFIED SURVIVES — brand tokens, site fonts and element animations all reach the published page, and both export paths emit them.
evidence: Tokens and font rules: publish emits siteTokensCSS + siteFontCSS at ExportEngine.ts:680-682, the single file at :257-260; both then add googleFontsHeadLinks so a named family is actually fetched (:820-823 and :516-522). Animations: collectUsedKeyframes scans the generated CSS and appends the matching @keyframes blocks — publish at ExportEngine.ts:690-692, single file at :283-285 — and every preset the inspector offers (AnimationEditor.tsx:21-53) has a bd-anim-* entry in animationKeyframes.ts:23-64, so the catalogues do not diverge.
fix: None. Recorded so the next pass does not re-derive it.
chain: Publish -> designTokens + animation styles -> siteTokensCSS / collectUsedKeyframes -> Published site -> brand colours, fonts and animations render

finding: VERIFIED SURVIVES — SEO meta and the Title template reach both the published page and the check that grades it; the editor field, the Prisma column and the renderer are one chain.
evidence: SeoScreen.tsx:67 writes settings.seo.metaTitleTemplate; BuildrikSyncProvider.ts:183 maps it to the Site.metaTitleTemplate column (prisma/schema.prisma:342) and :216 merges it back on load; publish.service.ts:76 grades that column ('SEO configured', warning only); SEOInjector.applyTitleTemplate (SEOInjector.ts:53-59) applies it to the page title, and both export paths call seoInjector.inject — publish at ExportEngine.ts:833 and the single file at :492-495. Language is read from the same block (resolveLanguage, SEOInjector.ts:71-73) by both.
fix: None. Recorded so the next pass does not re-derive it.
chain: Publish -> SiteSEO.metaTitleTemplate -> BuildrikSyncProvider patch -> Site column -> runPrePublishChecks + SEOInjector -> Published page title and the check agree

finding: VERIFIED SURVIVES — interactions reach the published page even though engine/interactions is one of the isolated modules; the export ships a WAAPI re-implementation rather than bundling GSAP.
evidence: renderPageElement emits data.interactions as the data-buildrick-interactions attribute (ExportEngine.ts:1040-1044) — necessary because toJSON does not carry the computed attribute — and the runtime is injected only when a page contains the marker (publish at :864-866, single file at :551-553). interactionRuntime.ts:206 wires all twelve triggers the inspector offers, and INTERACTION_EASINGS (:140-183) maps both easing vocabularies including the GSAP power1..power4 strings the inspector actually writes.
fix: None. Recorded so the next pass does not re-derive it.
chain: Publish -> Interaction[] on element.data -> data-buildrick-interactions + buildInteractionRuntimeScript -> Published site -> configured triggers play

finding: 'Download all' emits a duplicate stylesheet link, because the modal adds one to markup the engine already linked.
evidence: wrapInDocument already writes <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"> whenever cssStyle is 'external' (ExportEngine.ts:508-510). ExportModal.handleDownloadAll then adds a second one by string-replacing </head> for any non-embedded config (ExportModal.tsx:110-113). The companion CSS is also fired 100ms later through a second synthetic download (:116), which browsers commonly block as an unsolicited multi-file download.
fix: Drop the replace at ExportModal.tsx:112 — the engine already emitted the link — and hand 'Download all' to generateZip so the CSS travels in one file rather than a second timed download.
chain: Export -> ExportConfig.cssStyle external -> Download all -> two identical stylesheet links, CSS delivered by a timer

finding: Publish-panel and publish-flow screen gaps are already filed by the earlier wave — not re-filed here. What that wave did not cover is the data question this pass asked: which entities reach the live site.
evidence: Panel and flow states: W-D-01..W-D-26 (progress dead-ends, Connect Vercel loop, View live site, Try again, unpublish confirm, View log, cancelled outcome, role refusal, Fix-link targets). Published-version list and rollback: W-H-04, W-H-06, W-H-09, W-H-11, W-H-12, W-H-13, W-H-19, W-H-22, W-H-24, W-H-28. Publish diff: W-N-23, W-N-24, W-N-25. Flow reachability: W-P-02, W-P-22. Export modal controls: W-B-13, W-B-36, W-D-13. Ecommerce checkout config: W-O-26. MOD-C-01 is a second, independent break behind W-O-26 and does not duplicate it.
fix: None — pointer row so the dependency map can join this module's data findings to the existing screen findings.
chain: Publish -> screen states -> already filed in W-D / W-H / W-N / W-P -> this file adds the data-flow layer only

finding: A `blob:` image URL passes every filter in the publish path and ships verbatim into the live HTML, so an upload that failed silently in the editor becomes a permanently broken image on the customer's published site — and nothing anywhere checks for it.
evidence: The only attribute filter the publish writer applies is isSafeAttrValue (ExportEngine.ts:1034, and :328 on the single-file writer). For `src` that delegates to isSafeUrl(value, ALLOWED_SRC_SCHEMES) (sanitization.ts:83-86), and ALLOWED_SRC_SCHEMES is deliberately ALLOWED_URL_SCHEMES plus 'blob:' (sanitizationConfig.ts:271, with a comment explaining it exists so a just-uploaded image previews). An asset is BORN as a blob: URL (MediaManager.ts:942,955 URL.createObjectURL) and only becomes an https URL if remote sync succeeds; on failure the asset keeps the blob: src and is flagged localOnly (MediaManager.ts:1039-1042). Nothing downstream rescues it: AssetBundler has one non-test call site, inside generateZip (ExportEngine.ts:1093), so the publish path does no bundling; the payload is {path,html} only (packages/shared/schemas/publish.ts:20-31); the deploy file set is page HTML + robots.txt + sitemap.xml (lib/publish-files.ts:52-86) with no asset files; and runPrePublishChecks tests Vercel/pages/SEO/domain/empty-pages/favicon only (publish.service.ts:59-105) — there is no local-media or blob:-src check. A blob: URL is origin- and session-scoped, so on a visitor's browser it does not even issue a request.
fix: Refuse blob: on the EXPORT boundary specifically — isSafeAttrValue takes the tag and could take a mode, or exportPageToHtml could reject blob: srcs — and add a blocking pre-publish check for local-only assets, which MediaManager already tracks precisely (asset.localOnly, MediaManager.ts:1040, plus the retryQueue). Note three code comments assert the sanitizer already strips this on the way into the document (useMediaState.ts:265-270, useDropExecution.ts:126-130,256-260); for the publish path that is not true, and the comments are why nobody looked.
chain: Publish -> MediaAsset.src (blob:) -> isSafeAttrValue allows blob: for src -> published HTML -> visitor's browser -> broken image, no request, no warning, no pre-publish check

finding: The Optimize tab rewrites a library asset's src to a full base64 data URL that is never re-uploaded, so optimising an image inflates the published HTML toward the hard 2 MB per-page cap that rejects the publish outright.
evidence: MediaLibraryPanel.tsx:318-324 passes OptimizationPanel's result into updateAsset(id, { src }) where src is MediaOptimizer.optimize().dataUrl — a canvas toDataURL (MediaOptimizer.ts:95). MediaManager.updateAsset mirrors only folderId, name and altText to the server (MediaManager.ts:1160-1216); it never re-uploads bytes, so the local asset now holds the whole image inline while the server row still points at the old Blob URL. Publish then embeds that string in the page. The cap is enforced by a zod refine, not a friendly error: MAX_PAGE_HTML_BYTES = 2MB (packages/shared/schemas/publish.ts:12,25-31) and MAX_PUBLISH_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 16MB (:15), so a few optimised images turn into 'Page HTML exceeds 2097152 bytes'.
fix: Have the Optimize action round-trip through uploadFile the way the image editor already does (StudioPanels.tsx:378-389 fetches its data URL back into a File and uploads it), so the optimised bytes get a durable URL instead of riding inside the page.
chain: Publish -> optimised MediaAsset.src (data:) -> updateAsset without re-upload -> page HTML -> publishPageSchema 2MB refine -> publish rejected with a raw zod message

finding: Stock photos publish as hotlinks to Unsplash/Pexels — the library quietly saves its own copy but never repoints the element, so the live site depends on a third-party CDN the customer does not control.
evidence: useMediaState.ts:189 inserts photo.url from the stock proxy (services/stock/StockService.ts) directly as the element src, e.g. https://images.unsplash.com/photo-...?w=400. autoSaveStockToLibrary (useMediaState.ts:169-177, called at :211) uploads a copy to the media library afterwards but does not rewrite the element's src. The publish path copies attributes verbatim (ExportEngine.ts:1029-1037), and no bundling runs on that path (AssetBundler's only call site is generateZip, ExportEngine.ts:1093).
fix: Point the element at the library copy once autoSaveStockToLibrary resolves — the id is already in hand — so the published site serves its own asset.
chain: Publish -> stock photo URL -> element src (never repointed) -> published site -> images served by a third-party CDN, breakable outside the customer's control

finding: The ASSET_* events are declared with zero emitters and zero subscribers, which is why no module can react to an upload failing — the one signal a pre-publish media check would need.
evidence: events.ts:377-379 declares ASSET_UPLOADED, ASSET_DELETED and ASSET_SELECTED; the only other hits in src/ are the payload type declarations (shared/types/media.ts:843,859). This matches EVENT-GRAPH.json's 'never' set, which the brief already names as including the ASSET_* group. The live media bus is a separate namespace, MEDIA_EVENTS (shared/constants/media.ts), which is what MediaManager actually emits (e.g. MEDIA_EVENTS.UPLOAD_PROGRESS, MediaManager.ts:1036).
fix: Delete the three dead constants, and if a publish-time media gate is built (MOD-C-17) let it read MediaManager's localOnly/retryQueue state directly rather than reviving an unused event namespace.
chain: Publish -> asset upload fails -> (ASSET_* never emitted; MEDIA_EVENTS is a separate bus) -> Publish panel -> no pre-publish signal that media is local-only
